exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 1 and 2, find the change of variable $$\textbf{x} = P\textbf{y}$$ that transforms the quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ into $$\textbf{y}^{T}D\textbf{y}$$ as shown.
Hint: $$\textbf{x}$$ and $$\textbf{y}$$ must have the same number of coordinates, so the quadratic form shown here must have a coefficient of zero for $$y_{3}^{2}$$ .

In Exercises 3–6, find (a) the maximum value of $$Q(\textbf{x})$$ subject to the constraint $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1$$ , (b) a unit vector $$\textbf{u}$$ where this maximum is attained, and (c) the maximum of $$Q(\textbf{x})$$ subject to the constraints $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1$$ and $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{u} = 0$$ .

problem.paragraph: Let $$Q(\textbf{x}) = - 2x_{1}^{2} - x_{2}^{2} + 4x_{1}x_{2} + 4x_{2}x_{3}$$ . Find a unit vector $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$\textbf{\mathbb{R}}^{3}$$ at which $$Q(\textbf{x})$$ is maximized, subject to $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1$$ . [Hint: The eigenvalues of the matrix of the quadratic form $$Q$$ are $$2$$ , $$- 1$$ , and $$- 4$$ .]

Let $$Q(\textbf{x}) = 7x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} + 7x_{3}^{2} - 8x_{1}x_{2} - 4x_{1}x_{3} - 8x_{2}x_{3}$$ . Find a unit vector $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$\textbf{\mathbb{R}}^{3}$$ at which $$Q(\textbf{x})$$ is maximized, subject to $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1$$ . [Hint: The eigenvalues of the matrix of the quadratic form $$Q$$ are $$9$$ and $$- 3$$ .]

Find the maximum value of $$Q(\textbf{x}) = 7x_{1}^{2} + 3x_{2}^{2} - 2x_{1}x_{2}$$ , subject to the constraint $$x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} = 1$$ . (Do not go on to find a vector where the maximum is attained.)

Find the maximum value of $$Q(\textbf{x}) = - 3x_{1}^{2} + 5x_{2}^{2} - 2x_{1}x_{2}$$ , subject to the constraint $$x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} = 1.$$ (Do not go on to find a vector where the maximum is attained.)
Suppose $$\textbf{x}$$ is a unit eigenvector of a matrix $$A$$ corresponding to an eigenvalue $$3$$ . What is the value of $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ ?

Let $$\text{λ}$$ be any eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix $$A$$ . Justify the statement made in this section that $$m \leq \text{λ} \leq M$$ , where $$m$$ and $$M$$ are defined as in (2). [Hint: Find an $$\textbf{x}$$ such that $$\text{λ} = \textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ .]

Let $$A$$ be an $$n \times n$$ symmetric matrix, let $$M$$ and $$m$$ denote the maximum and minimum values of the quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ , where $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1,$$ and denote corresponding unit eigenvectors by $$\textbf{u}_{1}$$ and $$\textbf{u}_{n}$$ . The following calculations show that given any number $$t$$ between $$M$$ and $$m$$ , there is a unit vector $$\textbf{x}$$ such that $$t = \textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ . Verify that $$t = (1 - \alpha)m + \alpha M$$ for some number $$\alpha$$ between $$0$$ and $$1$$ . Then let $$\textbf{x} = \sqrt{1 - \alpha}\textbf{u}_{n} + \sqrt{\alpha}\textbf{u}_{1}$$ , and show that $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1$$ and $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x} = t$$ .

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 14–17, follow the instructions given for Exercises 3–6.

problem.paragraph: The matrix of the quadratic form is $$A = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . It is easy to find the eigenvalues, $$4$$ and $$2$$ , and corresponding unit eigenvectors, $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {1/\sqrt{2}} \\ {1/\sqrt{2}} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 1/\sqrt{2}} \\ {1/\sqrt{2}} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . So the desired change of variable is $$\textbf{x} = P\textbf{y}$$ , where $$P = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} {1/\sqrt{2}} & {- 1/\sqrt{2}} \\ {1/\sqrt{2}} & {1/\sqrt{2}} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . (A common error here is to forget to normalize the eigenvectors.) The new quadratic form is $$\textbf{y}^{T}D\textbf{y} = 4y_{1}^{2} + 2y_{2}^{2}$$ .

The maximum of $$Q(\textbf{x})$$ , for a unit vector $$\textbf{x}$$ , is $$4$$ and the maximum is attained at the unit eigenvector $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {1/\sqrt{2}} \\ {1/\sqrt{2}} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . [A common incorrect answer is $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ 0 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . This vector maximizes the quadratic form $$\textbf{y}^{T}D\textbf{y}$$ instead of $$Q(\textbf{x})$$ .]
